title: The Birch–Erdős representation function f_{p,q} increases and decreases infinitely often (Ding–Liu–Wang Conjecture 3)
source: Yuchen Ding, Honghu Liu and Zi Wang, “Note on a theorem of Birch and Erdős”, arXiv:2503.11676 (2025); J. Number Theory (2025), doi 10.1016/j.jnt.2025.07.009; Conjecture 3. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.11676
statement:
Let $f_{p,q}(n)$ be the Birch–Erdős representation function, with $p$ and $q$ relatively prime integers satisfying $q>p>2$. **Sign-change conjecture.** The sign of

$$
f_{p,q}(n+1)-f_{p,q}(n)
$$

changes infinitely often. The conjecture is presented as a possible example of the Chebyshev bias phenomenon; the source does not establish it.
summary: The conjecture holds: for all coprime q > p > 2, the difference f_{p,q}(n+1) − f_{p,q}(n) is strictly positive for infinitely many n and strictly negative for infinitely many n, where f_{p,q}(n) counts the representations of n as a sum of distinct numbers p^a q^b. Infinitely many increases follow from the authors' Corollary 3 (f is unbounded). The new part is the decreases: if f were eventually nondecreasing, a comparison at roots of unity would force certain twisted products over pure powers to vanish, while the exact product over all roots of unity gives a uniform lower bound; the contradiction needs p > 2 (for p = 2 the authors prove that f is monotone). Lean defines f by the source's literal representation count and proves both infinitely many strict increases and infinitely many strict decreases, with non-vacuity checks.
paste_summary: Proved. Ding, Liu and Wang (arXiv:2503.11676, Conjecture 3) conjectured that for coprime q > p > 2 the Birch–Erdős representation function f_{p,q}(n), which counts representations of n as sums of distinct p^a q^b, changes direction infinitely often. It has infinitely many strict increases (from the authors' asymptotic) and infinitely many strict decreases (by a root-of-unity argument that fails exactly at p = 2, where f is monotone).
caveat: The journal version (J. Number Theory, doi 10.1016/j.jnt.2025.07.009) and the one indexed citing paper (H. Liu, Period. Math. Hungar., doi 10.1007/s10998-026-00707-y) could not be read in full; arXiv v3 and the indexed journal preview still call the statement Conjecture 3, and the citing paper's abstract concerns a different question (reviewer's probability that it settles this conjecture: 0.02). The increases are the authors' own Corollary 3; the contribution is the decreases, a few compact paragraphs.
